about.title: Merced Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet floor with no sign, a broken step outside an apartment, a parking lot light that has been out for weeks. Falls like these happen in Merced more often than people expect, and the aftermath is rarely simple. Under California premises liability law, the question is usually not whether you fell but whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That element, called notice, is where most of these cases are decided. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Merced residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles slip, trip and fall claims in Merced County. Whether you were hurt at a store along G Street, a rental property off W 16th Street, or a publicly owned sidewalk, the attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery. Timing matters too: two years for most claims, and considerably less when a public entity owns the property.

whyChoose.title: Why Merced Residents Turn to LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorney you are connected with focuses on that question from day one: how long the condition existed, who was responsible for inspecting, and what records show.

items.title: Video disappears fast
items.desc: Most Merced stores, apartment complexes and parking lots overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. A prompt preservation letter can keep the recording of your fall from being erased before anyone reviews it.

items.title: Two deadlines, not one
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a premises claim in California, but if the property belongs to the City of Merced, the county or another public agency, the window to submit a formal claim is much shorter. Getting connected early protects both.

items.question: I fell on a sidewalk owned by the City of Merced or Merced County. Does that change my deadline?
items.answer: Yes, and significantly. When the property is owned by a public entity, California generally requires you to file an administrative claim with that agency first, typically within six months of the injury, before any lawsuit can proceed. Missing that step can end the case regardless of how clear the hazard was. This is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney quickly rather than waiting to see how your recovery goes.

items.question: The store says I should have been watching where I was walking. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California uses pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you, but it is not eliminated even if you are found mostly at fault. An attorney will look at whether the hazard was obvious, whether warnings were posted, and how long the owner let the condition sit. The store's opinion is not the final word.

items.question: What should I do right after a fall at a Merced business or rental property?
items.answer: Photograph the exact spot, including anything that caused the fall, before it gets cleaned or repaired. Ask for an incident report and the names of any witnesses, then get medical care even if the pain seems minor at first. If cameras were present, note their locations so a preservation request can go out promptly. LawProactive can connect you with a Merced attorney, free of charge, who can take those steps on your behalf.
